newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission competence struggle over porn on internet.
newsitem.headline: Commission competence struggle over porn on internet.

text.p: The European Commission's work to find ways of preventing the use of the Internet to spread paedophilia and child pornography has descended into a battle between European Commissioners over who is in charge.

Culture Commissioner Marcelino Oreja wants to broach the issue in a forthcoming green paper on new media services, but at his own admission the paper contains more questions than answers about how the goal should be achieved.

That position has not satisfied European Commission President Jacques Santer who -- responding to the public outcry after a Belgian paedophilia scandal -- wants answers and not just questions, EU officials say.

Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann, who EU officials say styles himself as Mr Information Society at the Commission, has drawn up his own, he says more concrete, paper and says that as the Commissioner responsible for new technology he is in charge.
As a result an already embattled Oreja is expected to see his green paper on new media services delayed by at least a week. He originally hoped it would be adopted on October 9.
"We all agree (about fighting paedophilia). The question is how to do it," a spokesman for Oreja said. "The idea is to do this without creating more problems."

The two commissioners could attempt to forge a common paper -- but this could be difficult as they are both coming from different directions. Bangemann has technology and industry on his mind, while Oreja must weigh the questions of cultural diversity and freedom of expression.

To complicate matters, Single Market Commissioner Mario Monti has a stake in the discussion -- he has responsibility for ensuring that the free flow of services in the information society is not impeded by regulation.
The row adds to Oreja's problems at a time Santer is not hiding his dissatisfaction at the way DG10 -- the directorate general for information -- is being run.
Director General of DG 10 Colette Flesch will be shunted at the end of the year to head the translation service, EU officials say.
They say Santer wants her position filled by one of his own men -- Commission spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas, who as director general would maintain his job as spokesman.

In addition, they say, Bangemann is itching to take over competence for what has been Oreja's most high-profile dossier - audiovisual policy, notably the television without frontiers directive, again on the grounds that the future questions of the audiovisual sector will revolve around technology.
The European Parliament is expected to fight against this as it considers cultural and not just technological questions will need to be addressed as ever before in the information age.
Oreja told Reuters in a recent interview that DG 10 would not lose any competences at the Commission during his lifetime as a Commissioner, although he did not object to taking on new ones.
